samples.question: The picture shows nine gray bars of equal width, evenly spaced and standing on one black baseline; only their heights differ. A single black bar stands on the same baseline to the left of the vertical black divider: that is the reference bar, and only its height matters. Read the nine gray bars from left to right. A pair of neighbouring gray bars is a RISE when the right bar of the pair is taller than the left bar by strictly more than the height of the reference bar; every other neighbouring pair is not a rise. A CHAIN is a group of consecutive gray bars in which every neighbouring pair inside the group is a rise, and the longest chain never contains more than five bars. A single gray bar with no rise on either side of it is a chain of one bar. The pale horizontal guide rows are decorative and carry no information. How many gray bars does the longest chain contain? Answer 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5.
